quick: 80 mg orally once daily (or 40 mg BID); T315I: 200 mg BID
On an empty stomach: no food for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after dosing.
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and after treatment per labeling
Do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
See full labeling; monitor renal function with diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration risk
See full labeling; dose-reduce in moderate-severe impairment for hepatically cleared agents

summary: Asciminib (Scemblix) is a first-in-class STAMP inhibitor for Philadelphia-chromosome-positive CML in chronic phase after 2+ TKIs, and for T315I-mutated disease. Allosteric myristoyl-pocket binding overcomes ATP-site mutations. Key toxicities are myelosuppression, pancreatitis (lipase/amylase monitoring), hypertension and cardiovascular events, and hypersensitivity.
indications: Ph-positive CML in chronic phase previously treated with 2 or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors
Ph-positive CML in chronic phase with the T315I mutation

dosage.d: 80 mg once daily (or 40 mg twice daily) continuously
dosage.t: Take on an empty stomach (no food 2 hours before and 1 hour after); swallow whole
dosage.n: No food effect tolerance - fasting is required

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Asciminib Specifically Targets the ABL Myristoyl Pocket (STAMP), locking BCR::ABL1 in an inactive conformation allosterically. Because it does not compete at the ATP site, it retains activity against many ATP-site resistance mutations including T315I.
preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

moderate: CYP3A4 substrates with narrow index (asciminib inhibits CYP3A4)
interactions.food: On an empty stomach: no food for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after dosing.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Severe abdominal pain radiating to the back with vomiting (pancreatitis) - seek emergency care
Chest pain, sudden weakness or speech change (cardiovascular event) - seek emergency care

counsel: Take on an empty stomach - no food 2 hours before and 1 hour after, or it will not work properly
Report severe stomach pain with vomiting (pancreas inflammation)
Report chest pain, swelling or severe headache; attend blood-pressure checks
Attend regular blood-count and leukaemia-transcript blood tests; use contraception
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: First STAMP inhibitor: binds the myristoyl pocket, not the ATP site - hence T315I activity
Fasting administration is mandatory (food markedly alters absorption)
Molecular (BCR::ABL1 transcript) monitoring, not just counts, judges response
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered on the same day unless near the next dose; do not double.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
